{{Infobox bilateral relations|Afghanistan–Pakistan sporting|Pakistan|Afghanistan|map= Pakistan Afghanistan locator.svg|filetype=svg}}
[[Pakistan]] and [[Afghanistan]] share a regional [[List of sports rivalries|sporting rivalry]] that extends into various sports, especially [[cricket]] and [[Association football|football]]. The rivalry is attributed to the [[Afghanistan–Pakistan relations|historical, cultural and political relationship]] between the neighbouring countries.

==History==
In Afghanistan, sporting contests against Pakistan are followed intensely.<ref name="TRT">{{cite news|url=https://www.trtworld.com/sport/cricket-politics-spices-up-ahead-of-pakistan-afghanistan-match-27879|title=Cricket: Politics spices up ahead of Pakistan-Afghanistan match|work=TRT World|date=28 June 2019|accessdate=4 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Monga">{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/an-opportunity-to-keep-the-afghanistan-pakistan-rivalry-dignified-1191500|title=An opportunity to keep the Afghanistan-Pakistan rivalry dignified|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=28 June 2019|accessdate=4 September 2022|first=Sidharth|last=Monga}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/afghanistan-celebrates-3-0-victory-over-pakistan-in-historic-football-match-in-front-of-buoyant-crowd-52933|title=Afghanistan celebrates 3-0 victory over Pakistan in historic football match in front of buoyant crowd|work=Hurriyet Daily News|date=21 August 2013|accessdate=4 September 2022}}</ref> The rivalry, stemming from geopolitical and cultural ties between the two states, has been compared in some aspects to the more longstanding, traditional [[India–Pakistan sports rivalries|archrivalry between India and Pakistan]] in sports.<ref name="Monga"/>

The two countries share a long and porous [[Durand Line|international border]] dating back to the 19th century, with a history of immigration and economic relations. People on both sides of the border, primarily the [[Pashtuns]], share ethnic and cultural ties.<ref name="Monga"/> However, at a political level, relations between both governments in the past have often been characterised as frosty, thus paving the way for a competitive rivalry in sporting encounters in recent times.<ref name="TRT"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-afghanistan-pakistan-soccer-idUKBRE97J0PW20130820|title=Afghanistan-Pakistan football match bright point in tumultuous history|work=Reuters|date=21 August 2013|accessdate=4 September 2022|first=Jessica|last=Donati}}</ref>

==Olympics==
[[Afghanistan at the Olympics|Afghanistan]] made its first appearance at the [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympics]] in [[1936 Summer Olympics|1936]], while [[Pakistan at the Olympics|Pakistan]]'s first appearance was in [[1948 Summer Olympics|1948]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/afghanistan|title=Afghanistan|work=International Olympic Committee|accessdate=23 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Nalwala">{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/news/how-many-pakistan-olympic-medals-won|title=Pakistan's Olympic medals: Hockey team's domination is clear|work=International Olympic Committee|accessdate=23 September 2022|first=Ali Asgar|last=Nalwala}}</ref> Pakistan have won 11 Olympic medals since 1956, including four golds.<ref name="Nalwala"/> Afghanistan have won two bronze medals, in 2008 and 2012, with ''[[The Guardian]]'' reporting that there was "elation that Afghanistan had bettered" their medal tally against Pakistan in the [[2012 Summer Olympics|2012]] games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/aug/13/afghanistan-olympics-bronze-rohullah-nikpai|title=Afghanistan unites behind Olympic success – and beating Pakistan|work=The Guardian|date=14 August 2012|accessdate=24 September 2022|first=Emma|last=Graham-Harrison|quote=Two weeks of competition brought the glory of the country's second ever medal, dashed hopes of a third, triumph in getting one over on its powerful neighbour Pakistan, and anger over the role of an old enemy – corruption... There was also elation that Afghanistan had bettered their richer and more powerful neighbour Pakistan, which has long been resented for interference in Afghan affairs.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409165736/https://amp.theguardian.com/world/2012/aug/13/afghanistan-olympics-bronze-rohullah-nikpai|archivedate=9 April 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Head to head===
Pakistani and Afghan athletes have only directly competed against each other at the Olympics in men's [[Wrestling at the Summer Olympics|wrestling]] events. Every time Pakistani athletes have come out on top. In 1960, Pakistan's [[Muhammad Akhtar (wrestler)|Muhammad Akhtar]] defeated Afghanistan's [[Mohammad Ebrahim Khedri]] in the first round of the [[Wrestling at the 1960 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle featherweight|freestyle featherweight]] category by 4–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/124294|title=Featherweight, Freestyle (≤62 kilograms), Men|work=Olympedia|accessdate=24 September 2022}}</ref> In the [[Wrestling at the 1960 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle middleweight|freestyle middleweight]] category, Pakistan's [[Faiz Muhammad]] beat Afghanistan's [[Mohammad Asif Kohkan]] in the third round by 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/124446|title=Middleweight, Freestyle (≤79 kilograms), Men|work=Olympedia|accessdate=24 September 2022}}</ref> In the [[Wrestling at the 1960 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle heavyweight|freestyle heavyweight]] category, Pakistan's [[Muhammad Nazir (wrestler, born 1930)|Muhammad Nazir]] also won against Afghanistan's [[Nizamuddin Subhani]] in the second round by 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/124528|title=Heavyweight, Freestyle (>87 kilograms), Men|work=Olympedia|accessdate=24 September 2022}}</ref>

In 1972, Pakistan's [[Muhammad Yaghoub]] and Afghanistan's [[Shakar Khan Shakar]] drew in the second round of the [[Wrestling at the 1972 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle 74 kg|freestyle 74 kg]] event.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/126604?id=332414|title=Welterweight, Freestyle (≤74 kilograms), Men|work=Olympedia|accessdate=24 September 2022}}</ref>

===History===
[[Cricket in Afghanistan]] was popularised by [[Afghans in Pakistan|Afghan expatriates]] who learnt the sport while living in Pakistan in the 1980s and 1990s, during the [[Soviet–Afghan War|post-Soviet invasion]] era.<ref name="TRT"/><ref name="Monga"/> Most members of the early [[Afghanistan national cricket team]] grew up in northwest Pakistan and participated in the country's domestic cricket structure, making use of cricket facilities in [[Peshawar]] with the support of the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB).<ref name="ET">{{cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/159156/afghanistan-cricket-teams-play-in-pakistan|title=Afghanistan cricket teams play in Pakistan|work=The Express Tribune|date=29 April 2011|accessdate=4 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Monga"/> It was during this time that the [[Afghanistan Cricket Board|Afghanistan Cricket Federation]] (now ACB) was also founded, in 1995.<ref name="Wigmore">{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/tim-wigmore-taj-malik-the-man-who-gave-afghanistan-their-mojo-772985|title=The man who gave Afghanistan their mojo|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=22 August 2014|accessdate=4 September 2022|first=Tim|last=Wigmore}}</ref> The ACF received recognition from the [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC) in 2001.<ref name="Wigmore"/>

Several future cricketers representing Afghanistan emerged from Peshawar's club cricket scene, establishing an Afghan cricket club to compete against other local Pakistani sides in the 1990s.<ref name="Wigmore"/> Afghanistan fielded their cricket team in Pakistan's domestic setup for the first time in the 2001–02 season, participating in the second division of the [[Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] where they drew two and lost three of their five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://static.espncricinfo.com/db/ARCHIVE/2001-02/PAK_LOCAL/QEAII/SCORECARDS/POOL-B/|title=Pool B - Scorecards|work=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="SMH">{{cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/afghanistan-to-compete-in-pakistans-domestic-league-20030820-gdh9on.html|title=Afghanistan to compete in Pakistan's domestic league|work=Sydney Morning Herald|date=20 August 2003|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref> They returned for the Cornelius Trophy in the 2002–03 season, drawing one and losing three matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://static.espncricinfo.com/db/ARCHIVE/2002-03/PAK_LOCAL/CORNELIUS/SCORECARDS/POOL-D/|title=Cornelius Trophy 2002-03 (Associations)|work=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref> In the 2003–04 season, they made an appearance in the PCB's inter-district tournament in Peshawar, where they registered their lone victory against [[Swabi]], drew twice and lost two matches.<ref name="SMH"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://static.espncricinfo.com/db/ARCHIVE/2003-04/PAK_LOCAL/INTD-SENIOR/SCORECARDS/PESHAWAR-REGION/POOL-A/|title=Inter District Senior, 2003-04 (Peshawar Region) Scorecards - Pool A|work=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref>

The Afghanistan national team was coached by former Pakistani cricketers [[Kabir Khan (cricketer)|Kabir Khan]] and [[Rashid Latif]] in its initial years.<ref name="TRT"/><ref name="ET"/> During this period, a number of Afghan international cricketers made appearances for Pakistani domestic outfits in the first-class circuit.<ref name="Monga"/><ref name="Farooq">{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/afghanistan-sign-up-for-pakistan-support-626326|title=Afghanistan sign up for Pakistan support|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=22 March 2013|accessdate=5 September 2022|first=Umar|last=Farooq}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/aaron-summers-set-to-be-first-australian-to-play-pakistan-domestic-cricket-1245211|title=Aaron Summers set to be first Australian to play Pakistan domestic cricket|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=26 December 2020|accessdate=5 September 2022|first=Danyal|last=Rasool}}</ref> In 2010, Afghanistan competed at the [[Cricket at the 2010 Asian Games|Asian Games]], a non-ICC [[Twenty20|T20]] event hosted by China, where they defeated a second-string Pakistan side [[Cricket at the 2010 Asian Games – Men#Semifinals|by 22 runs in the semi-finals]] in what was considered an upset.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asian-games-men-s-cricket-competition-2010-11-485152/afghanistan-vs-pakistan-1st-semi-final-485182/match-report|title=Afghanistan upset Pakistan to reach final|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=25 November 2010|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref> In May 2011, the Afghan side embarked on a tour of Pakistan to partake in a three-match [[List A cricket|limited overs]] series against [[Pakistan A cricket team|Pakistan A]], where they were whitewashed by the home side 3–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/afghanistan-tour-of-pakistan-2011-515687/pakistan-a-vs-afghanistan-3rd-unofficial-odi-515691/match-report|title=Pakistan A sweep series with hard-fought win|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=29 May 2011|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Farooq"/> They followed this up with another tour in September to participate in Pakistan's domestic [[2011–12 National T20 Cup|National T20 Cup]] in Karachi as the [[Afghan Cheetahs]], but had another poor outing, [[Afghan Cheetahs#Fixtures and results|losing all three]] of their matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/team/match_results_year.html?class=6;id=4947;type=team|title=Afghan Cheetahs|work=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref>

On 10 February 2012, Afghanistan played a one-off [[One Day International]] (ODI) match against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] at [[Sharjah Cricket Stadium|Sharjah]], the [[Afghan cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2011–12|first ever official game between the two sides]] and also the first ever ODI between an [[List of International Cricket Council members|Affiliate]] and a [[Test cricket#Teams with Test status|Test]]-playing nation.<ref name="Sundar">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-england-2012/content/current/story/552656.html|title=A landmark in the Afghanistan journey|date=9 February 2012|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]|accessdate=5 September 2022|first=Nitin|last=Sundar}}</ref> Billed as a historic occasion for Afghan cricket, the game was won comfortably by Pakistan by seven wickets with 13 overs to spare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/716713|title=Afghanistan's 17-year journey to Test cricket|work=International Cricket Council|date=13 June 2018|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/334910/cricket-even-taliban-seduced-by-afghanistan-success-story|title=Cricket: Even Taliban seduced by Afghanistan success story|work=The Express Tribune|date=11 February 2012|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref>

In [[Afghan cricket team in Pakistan in 2013|February 2013]], Afghanistan visited Pakistan to play a series of limited-overs matches against the Pakistan A team and some regional sides. They played five one-dayers and a Twenty20 at three venues around the country. They won their first limited overs game against [[Hyderabad cricket team (Pakistan)|Hyderabad]]–[[Karachi cricket teams|Karachi]] by nine wickets,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/afghanistan-tour-of-pakistan-2012-13-603369/hyderabad-pakistan-and-karachi-vs-afghanistan-603396/match-report|title=Shehzad, Hotak give Afghanistan A big win|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=6 February 2013|accessdate=5 February 2022}}</ref> but lost their matches against [[Bahawalpur cricket team|Bahawalpur]]–[[Multan cricket team|Multan]] and [[Faisalabad cricket team|Faisalabad]]–[[Rawalpindi cricket team|Rawalpindi]]. In their matches against Pakistan A, they were clean swept by the Pakistani side 2–0 in the one day series and 1–0 in the T20 series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/afghanistan-tour-of-pakistan-2012-13-603369|title=Afghanistan tour of Pakistan 2012/2013|work=ESPNcricinfo|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref> In March, the PCB and ACB inked a two-year memorandum of understanding allowing Afghanistan to use Pakistan's cricket facilities such as the National Cricket Academy and seek technical assistance for the purpose of further developing Afghan cricket.<ref name="Farooq"/> Later in December that year, Pakistan and Afghanistan [[Sri Lankan cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2013–14#Pakistan vs Afghanistan: Only T20I|faced each other in a one-off T20I]] in Sharjah, where Pakistan prevailed with a six wicket victory with a ball to spare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/afghanistan-tour-of-united-arab-emirates-2013-14-657629/afghanistan-vs-pakistan-only-t20i-657631/match-report|title=Pakistan prevail in last-over finish|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=8 December 2013|accessdate=5 September 2022}}</ref> Since then, the two sides have clashed in the ODI and T20I formats on multiple occasions. In World Cup 2023 Afghanistan beat Pakistan in a match played on October 23, 2023. [[Ibrahim Zadran]], who was awarded player of the match award, dedicated the win to “people who are sent from Pakistan back home to Afghanistan”. His statement was considered controversial especially from Pakistan side amid the decision from Pakistan to deport all illegal Afghan citizens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rare public joy in Kabul after Afghanistan's World Cup win over Pakistan |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/10/24/rare-public-joy-in-kabul-after-afghanistans-world-cup-win-over-pakistan |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=www.aljazeera.com |language=en}}</ref>

====ICC tournaments====
The teams have met on three occasions in ICC tournaments, with Pakistan winning two of these meetings and Afghanistan winning one.

====ACC tournaments====
In [[Asian Cricket Council]] (ACC) tournaments, both sides have met on five occasions. Pakistan have won on three occasions, while Afghanistan have won two games.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dawlatzai |first=Mohammad Kawsar |date=2020-12-25 |title=India and Pakistan Rivalry in Afghanistan: A new Imperialism in the Making |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.31841/kjssh.2021.34 |journal=Kardan Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities |doi=10.31841/kjssh.2021.34 |issn=2616-8707}}</ref>

==Football==
The national teams of [[Pakistan national football team|Pakistan]] and [[Afghanistan national football team|Afghanistan]] have competed against each other in [[association football]] on six occasions in history; twice in the [[SAFF Championship]] and five times in international [[Exhibition game|friendlies]]. Pakistan have dominated the match-ups, winning four of these games, while Afghanistan have won two games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=World Football Elo Ratings: Pakistan |url=http://eloratings.net/Pakistan |website=www.eloratings.net}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=World Football Elo Ratings: Afghanistan |url=https://www.eloratings.net/Afghanistan |website=www.eloratings.net}}</ref> Both teams first met at the 1976 [[Afghanistan Republic Day Festival Cup]], where the A team of Afghanistan won by 1–0,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Afghanistan Republic Day Festival Cup (Kabul, Afghanistan) |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesj/jasson76.html#1976 |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=www.rsssf.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Graham-Harrison |first=Emma |date=2013-08-20 |title=Football match allows Afghanistan to forget its woes for 90 minutes |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2013/aug/20/afghanistan-pakistan-football-match |access-date=2025-04-05 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-08-20 |title=In First Meeting Since 1970s, Afghanistan Tops Pakistan In Soccer |url=https://www.wlrn.org/2013-08-20/in-first-meeting-since-1970s-afghanistan-tops-pakistan-in-soccer |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=WLRN |language=en}}</ref> with [[Mohammad Saber Rohparwar]] scoring the lone goal on a corner kick minutes before game's end.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hodge |first=Nathan |date=2013-08-20 |title=A Pitch Battle Unites Afghans, Pakistanis |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/a-pitch-battle-unites-afghans-pakistanis-1377027769 |access-date=2025-03-03 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Afghanistan and Pakistan Braced to Face-Off in Kabul for First Time in 37 Years |url=https://tolonews.com/sports/afghanistan-and-pakistan-braced-face-kabul-first-time-37-years |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=TOLOnews |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Afghan Footballers Return From Abroad Ahead of Pakistan Match |url=https://tolonews.com/sports/afghan-footballers-return-abroad-ahead-pakistan-match |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=TOLOnews |language=en}}</ref> Because of rising tensions between the two countries in the 1970s, Afghan president [[Mohammad Daoud Khan]] handed each player 5,000 afghanis as a celebration and gift for their victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan National Team's Return to Kabul Echoes 1976 Jashen Celebration |url=https://tolonews.com/opinion/pakistan-national-teams-return-kabul-echoes-1976-jashen-celebration |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=TOLOnews |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Latifi |first=Ali M. |title=Politics kicked aside in Afghan football game |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2013/8/22/politics-kicked-aside-in-afghan-football-game |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref> Both teams met again at the [[1976 Quaid-e-Azam International Tournament]] the same year where Pakistan avenged by winning by the same score, with forward Afzal Qasim scoring the winning goal in the eighth minute after the kick off.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quaid-E-Azam International Cup (Pakistan) |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesq/quaid-e-azam.html#76 |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=www.rsssf.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan's National Team Arrives in Kabul |url=https://tolonews.com/sports/pakistans-national-team-arrives-kabul |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=TOLOnews |language=en}}</ref> A Pakistani selection named Shaheen FC again participated in the Afghan tournament in 1977.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-08-21 |title=Football: Afghanistan win first home game against Pakistan since 1977 |url=https://english.alarabiya.net/sports/2013/08/21/Football-Afghanistan-beat-Pakistan-in-first-such-match-since-1977 |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=Al Arabiya English |language=en}}</ref>

The ensuing civil war and political instability in Afghanistan prevented the two sides from meeting again until 2003.<ref name="RFERL222">{{cite news |last=Bezhan |first=Frud |date=21 August 2013 |title=Historic Soccer Match Brings Unity To Afghanistan |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/afghanistan-pakistan-soccer-unity-celebration/25082095.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905151801/https://www.rferl.org/a/afghanistan-pakistan-soccer-unity-celebration/25082095.html |archive-date=5 September 2022 |accessdate=4 September 2022 |work=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty}}</ref> Contests against Pakistan generate much enthusiasm amongst Afghan football fans on account of their mutual relations and have been referred to as a "[[List of association football rivalries|rivalry]]",<ref name="RFERL">{{cite news |last=Bezhan |first=Frud |date=21 August 2013 |title=Historic Soccer Match Brings Unity To Afghanistan |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/afghanistan-pakistan-soccer-unity-celebration/25082095.html |accessdate=4 September 2022 |work=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=20 August 2013 |title=Afghanistan beat Pakistan 3-0 in Kabul friendly |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-23766790 |accessdate=12 September 2022 |work=BBC News}}</ref> although the interest in Pakistan toward the rivalry in general is more muted.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 August 2013 |title=Confident Pakistan ready for historic Afghanistan clash |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1037101 |accessdate=12 September 2022 |work=Dawn}}</ref>
